title: Complete partial signed-Pauli contracts with literal Clifford lifts
body:
Partial native-chart constraints can agree on every unsigned Pauli label and commutator yet have no Clifford realization: `X→X, Z→Z, Y→−Y` would change the central relation `X Z Y=−iI`. This adds a complete all-size signed compatibility criterion, constructs an actual dyadic Clifford word using at most two transvections per independent label plus a Pauli correction, and counts all projective completions exactly.

The emitted words are bound to the actual retained native compiler's `tableau`, `compile_word`, exact-column `replay`, anchor and tensor-phase functions. Eleven focused compiler cases include a three-bit full-column check and a nine-bit signed-tableau/anchor check. The compiler is a pinned dependency, with its original NOTICE and LICENSE retained in the export.

Independent literal Pauli-monomial closure reconstructs all 24 one-qubit and 11,520 two-qubit projective Cliffords. For canonical representatives of every source-span symplectic type, all 15,302 distinct target restrictions match exact multiplicities, and every emitted word is independently evaluated gate by gate. Mathematical and malformed-input rejections include the central-phase obstruction, wrong commutators and noninjective label data.

This is a scoped written proof with finite corroboration. The theorem holds for arbitrary n; executable calibration is explicitly limited to n≤9. Projective feasibility leaves global phase free: the chosen word is not automatically equal to a separately supplied target without its amplitude anchor. Minimum paid rank, a profitable completed caller, owners, physical movement, precision, stock and outer supplier admission remain open. No new κ; selected κ stays 0.00302015. No independent human or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

Credit Dugongue's #4841 native compiler, Cao Yifan/intqwq #4610, Cinna Davis, zxv, Jacob Alan Sussman, the retained native/Clifford/owner/compiler lineage and classical Witt/Clifford structure. Prepared for JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19140242 .
